trust_decision.summary: Zip::Entry#extract decides whether an entry may be written to the filesystem by comparing the absolute extract path against the destination directory with a bare String#start_with? prefix test; the only boundary logic is that prefix test plus the root-directory special case added by the fix (lib/zip/entry.rb:290-296).

landing_point.why: name_safe? is the only method in the tree documented as the path-traversal guard ('Is the name a relative path, free of `..` patterns that could lead to path traversal attacks?', entry.rb:230-232) and the existing suite for this area lives in test/path_traversal_test.rb, so an engineer reading only 'rubyzip path traversal vulnerability' lands there or on the tests; the actual changed line is 60 lines lower, in the destination-path comparison inside extract at entry.rb:293.

fix_sites.entry_point: Zip::Entry#extract (lib/zip/entry.rb:289); the same guard is reached through Zip::File#extract (lib/zip/file.rb:282-287), which delegates and needs no separate edit

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can quote the doc comment 'the caller is responsible for making sure `destination_directory` is safe, if it is passed' (lib/zip/entry.rb:287-288) and call any destination-relative escape the caller's bug, but the advisory's own fix puts that responsibility in the library; there is no second site or uncovered route here for the argument to protect.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Entries whose stored name is absolute ('/tmp/moo', '/tmp/file.txt') are legitimately re-rooted under destination_directory by File.join (entry.rb:291) and their contents are written inside it; a name-based rejection -- the dead name_safe? helper (entry.rb:233-241), or raising EntryNameError for '/'-prefixed names where the parser assigns @name (entry.rb:514) -- skips or aborts those entries and breaks the existing suite.

O6_input_shapes: entry name with '../' segments that resolve into a sibling directory sharing the destination's name prefix (e.g. '../out_evil/breakout.txt' with destination_directory 'out')
caller-supplied entry_path that differs from the stored entry name (first argument of Zip::Entry#extract / Zip::File#extract, e.g. test/file_options_test.rb:157-159)
destination_directory as an absolute path, a relative path, or nil (nil means '.', entry.rb:290)
destination_directory equal to the filesystem root '/' (the added '|| dest_dir == File::SEPARATOR' clause keeps root extraction working)

O7_producer.where: lib/zip/entry.rb:506-526 (central-directory name read at entry.rb:514; local-header equivalent at entry.rb:373), reached from lib/zip/central_directory.rb:37

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A `Zip::File#extract_all(destination_directory:)` convenience that loops entries and writes each through a private helper instead of calling Entry#extract
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The README teaches callers to write exactly this per-entry loop themselves (README.md:214-219), and extract-all is the standard convenience in zip libraries; a maintainer adding one would join destination_directory + entry.name in the new helper and could repeat or forget the prefix check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A revived `name_safe?` gate used by a new public entry point (e.g. `Entry#extract_verified`) that validates the entry name rather than the resolved destination path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: name_safe? is dead code at the pinned commit but carries a doc comment claiming exactly this protection (entry.rb:230-232), so 'finishing' that work is a natural maintainer move -- and a name check cannot see destination-directory escapes or entry_path overrides.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A streaming `extract_all` / `extract_current` on Zip::InputStream that writes each entry to disk while walking the archive
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The README advertises InputStream as the fast path and shows the get_next_entry loop (README.md:232-249), so an extract-while-streaming helper is an obvious addition that would sit outside Zip::Entry#extract.

O9_family: path traversal (CWE-22): relative-path escape out of a caller-supplied destination directory via an insufficient string-prefix comparison

O10_build.toolchain: Ruby >= 3.0 (rubyzip.gemspec:29); bundler + rake + minitest, dev deps minitest ~> 5.25, rake ~> 13.2, rubocop, simplecov; `bundle exec rake test` (Rakefile:10-13), CI matrix in .github/workflows/tests.yml:11
O10_build.project_tests: test/path_traversal_test.rb (14 tests: leading slashes, '..' entries, file/dir symlinks, absolute names, tilde names) plus test/file_extract_test.rb, test/file_extract_directory_test.rb and test/file_options_test.rb all exercise extract and the destination_directory guard

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Validate the entry name instead of the resolved path -- gate extract on the existing name_safe? (lib/zip/entry.rb:233) or raise EntryNameError for '/'-prefixed names in read_c_dir_entry -- which silently skips absolute-named entries that must still be re-rooted under destination_directory (test/path_traversal_test.rb:41-50, 156-167).

out_of_scope_notes: The pinned-commit series also carries unrelated central-directory hardening (entry-count limit, stop-on-first-error, SecureRandom) in lib/zip/central_directory.rb; that is outside this advisory's extraction protection and was not pursued.
